execution: Five sequential fresh processes after all task builds and tests exited; each pinned to CPU 0.
measurement: warm_measure reuses a constructed circle and directly requests native filled area and bounds under STRICT, plus report point count; it does not use the Polygon measurement cache. construct_and_measure adds the complete requested report-ring construction. Source-via measurement includes file reading, parsing, source-native construction and classification of the independent analytic interior point on both layers.
oracles: Each circle has center (1,1), radius 1, exact area pi, and native bounds [0,0,2,2]. Initial/final observations are checked. Fresh repeated report rings retain identical coordinate counts, logical coordinate-payload bytes, and FNV-1a checksums over f64 bit patterns. The via row checks feature count and native membership, not serialized report bytes.
million_sample_case: All 1,000,001 closed report coordinates are retained. The row records 16,000,016 logical coordinate bytes, not a process allocation count.
replay: Copy this directory to a temporary location, update manifest dependency paths to the checkout, build --offline --release, and run with HYPERDRC_CIRCLE_ITERATIONS=100. run-probe.py records the five pinned trials; use a newly identified binary hash for a replay.
limitations: The fixtures are a capability cost probe, not a statistical regression bound, end-to-end throughput result, or cross-library comparison.
Scalar/kernel caches may already be warm in construct_and_measure; it is not a cold-process allocator or precision-refinement benchmark.
Observed warm and small-fixture times varied substantially across trials. Every trial is retained; no stable general speedup is claimed.
Report checksum traversal and exact circle oracle comparisons are outside the timed circle loops. Via oracle comparisons are inside its load_and_classify loop.
Peak RSS describes the whole process and executable size describes this linked probe; no allocation count, retained-heap bound, or library-size delta is asserted.
